RoomType.rationale: TurretOperatorWeak declares RoomType.Monster; the sim's turret_operator sits in weak_keys under the same act's rooms, which run.py treats as RoomType.MONSTER at combat entry -- matches.

IsWeak.rationale: TurretOperatorWeak overrides IsWeak => true. The sim has no is_weak field on Encounter itself; 'weakness' is externalized to which bucket the room generator draws from (rooms.py's ActRooms.weak_keys, drawn only for the act's opening weak-encounter rooms per num_weak_encounters in actmap.py). turret_operator is listed only in weak_keys, never normal/elite/boss_keys, which reproduces the same selection behaviour by a different mechanism -- same room-type classification, same act placement.

AllPossibleMonsters.rationale: C#'s AllPossibleMonsters array literal is [LivingShield, TurretOperator] (ModelDb.Monster<LivingShield>() first); the sim's monster_classes list is the same two classes. Fixed, always-spawning roster -- no possible divergence.

GenerateMonsters.rationale: C#'s GenerateMonsters returns (LivingShield, null) then (TurretOperator, null) -- LivingShield FIRST, matching its own AllPossibleMonsters order. Sim's monster_classes = [LivingShield, TurretOperator], same order, preserved by create_monsters' list comprehension into combat.enemies. Neither tuple carries a slot name on either side (monster_slots left at its default empty tuple, so slot_name stays None), and TurretOperatorWeak declares no Slots row at all (inherits EncounterModel.Slots = empty), so there is no row for LivingShield/TurretOperator to be re-sorted against even in the game -- the C# CombatManager.AddCreature guard (`creature.SlotName != null`) never fires for this encounter either. Zero RNG draws in GenerateMonsters on both sides. Roster, order, slot(-lessness) and draw-count all match.

ShouldReceiveCombatHooks.maps_to: the Encounter dataclass (sts2_rl/monsters/base.py) is never registered as a hook listener; only Monster instances register themselves
ShouldReceiveCombatHooks.rationale: Same structural fact as every unit in this batch.

guards.what: MinGoldReward/MaxGoldReward -- not overridden, inherits the Monster ladder (10-20) x Poverty multiplier
guards.rationale: sts2_rl/rewards.py GOLD_REWARD_RANGES[RoomType.MONSTER] = (10, 20) and TURRET_OPERATOR_WEAK sets neither min_gold nor max_gold -- matches (weak encounters use the same Monster ladder as normal ones; TurretOperatorWeak overrides only IsWeak, not the gold accessors). Poverty/ascension scaling out of scope per PROMPT.md.

TurretOperatorWeak does not override ShouldGiveRewards, so the base true stands (weak encounters do give rewards, unlike e.g. the Battleworn Dummy training fights). Encounter.should_give_rewards defaults True and TURRET_OPERATOR_WEAK leaves it unset -- matches.
